title: Explicit pin surface and conflict resolution for tag/semver/commit-hash
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers need deterministic model selection for production inference. They currently use a mix of tags (channels), semver ranges, and commit hashes. Ambiguity arises when multiple pin selectors are provided or when a pinned selector maps to multiple compatible artifacts (e.g., same tag on multiple releases). The runtime must guarantee deterministic resolution, clear audit trail, safe rollback behavior, and a developer-friendly API/SDK surface.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API/SDK accepts pin selectors: tag:<name>, semver:<range>, hash:<commit>. 2) Deterministic resolution order implemented and documented. 3) SDK and server return explicit resolution metadata (resolved_ref, resolution_path, confidence). 4) Audit logs contain original selector, resolved artifact id, and resolver version. 5) Rollback and canary semantics defined and implemented for pinned routes. 6) Backwards-compatible: existing non-pinned requests continue to use current latest mapping. 7) E2E tests and migration playbook created.
design_decisions: 1) Resolution precedence: hash > exact semver (e.g., 1.2.3) > semver range > tag. Rationale: most-specific (hash) is deterministic, semver exact pins an exact release, ranges are best-effort, tags are mutable channels. 2) When multiple artifacts match an input (e.g., semver range matches multiple builds with same semver metadata), resolver selects the artifact with the highest build timestamp and surfaces a warning. 3) If a hash is supplied but not found in the active catalog, fail fast with HTTP 404 and a clear error code (pin_not_found). 4) If a semver range resolves to a prerelease when a stable exists, prefer stable unless client opts into prerelease with a flag. 5) Resolution favors reproducibility: resolved_ref is an immutable model artifact id (artifact:<sha256>). 6) SDK convenience: allow composite pin strings ("pin=semver:^1.2.0;tag=stable") — resolver evaluates per precedence and returns the chosen result with explanation. 7) Introduce a resolver-version header in responses (X-Model-Resolver-Version) so any changes are visible in telemetry.
rollback_and_canary: - Canary: route-level pins can be applied to a subset via rollout policy (e.g., 10% traffic to semver:^2.2.0). Traffic is routed deterministically by request hashing. - Rollback: a route pinned by semver can be rolled back to previous resolved_ref by promoting a prior artifact id; API includes an explicit 'promote' action that records the change in audit logs. - Safety: automatic fallback disabled by default for pinned routes; operators can enable 'fallback_to_compatible' flag which allows semantic fallback but records a warning and increments an alert metric.
observability_and_audit: - All resolution events emit a 'model_resolution' event: {request_id, selector_list, chosen_resolved_ref, resolver_version, timestamp, reason}. - Console drives a 'Pin resolution' timeline on deployment pages with clickable entries linking to artifact and PRs. - Add resolver metrics: resolution_latency_ms, resolution_conflicts, resolution_failures_pin_not_found. - Audit retention: 90 days for developer plan, 365+ for enterprise (configurable).
backwards_compatibility_plan: Existing clients that omit model_pin continue to receive the current mapping behavior. For SDKs, default modelPin param is null unless explicitly passed. We will ship server-side resolver v1 behind a feature flag and run a 2-week dogfood period. Notify customers via changelog and a migration guide that explains explicit pin benefits and changes.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for resolver precedence permutations (20+ cases). - Integration tests against model-catalog staging with synthetic artifacts to simulate tag drift and semver collisions. - E2E perf test to ensure resolution adds <5ms median latency. - Chaos test: simulate catalog unavailability and verify pinned-route behavior according to 'fallback_to_compatible' flag. - QA checklist: API errors, telemetry, SDK binding, console timeline rendering.
